learning_outcomes.text: Possess basic knowledge of the profession.
Ability to learn to work autonomously.
Possess knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.
Ability to mathematically conceptualize graphic entities and geometric transformations, as well as develop modeling and simulation processes in computer-aided product design and engineering.
Ability for the creation and interpretation of technical documentation, including technical drawings for project development and documentation.
Ability to model, simulate, and manage product data using CAD/CAE tools from a life-cycle perspective.
Possess basic knowledge for generating functional and technological design criteria.
Ability to create, manipulate, and modify 3D CAD geometry.
Ability to perform mechanical assemblies by restricting the degrees of freedom of previously modeled components.
Ability to validate designs using CAE (Computer Aided Engineering) tools.
Ability to obtain standardized drawings of said designs.
Acquire theoretical content related to design, fundamentals of CAD systems, and computational geometry.
Develop spatial perception and visualization, fundamental for the creation, transmission, and representation of designs and projects in engineering.
Apply general theoretical fundamentals using the notable possibilities offered by new technologies encompassed in Computer-Aided Design (CAD).

syllabus_topics: Block I. Bases of Computer-Aided Design.
Topic 1. Fundamentals of Industrial Design.
Topic 2. Introduction to Computer-Aided Design (CAD).
Topic 3. Computer-Aided Engineering.
Topic 4. CAE Workflow. Case of stress analysis.
Topic 5. Fundamentals of CAD systems.
Topic 6. Geometry and visualization in CAD systems.
Topic 7. Computational geometry in CAD systems.
Topic 8. Reverse Engineering and design quality control.
Block II: 3D geometric modeling using parametric design software SolidWorks.
Topic 1. Introduction to the working environment of a parametric 3D CAD software.
Topic 2. Drawing, editing, and visualization tools.
Topic 3. 3D Modeling. Parts.
Topic 4. Assembly of 3D part sets.
Topic 5. Production of 2D technical drawings.
Topic 6. 3D Modeling. Sheet metal module.
Topic 7. 3D Modeling. Structures and welded parts module.
Topic 8. Help, query, library, and collaborative work tools.
Block III: Validation of geometric design using CAE tools.
Topic 1. Stress analysis of 2D and 3D bar structures (truss type).
Topic 2. Stress analysis of beams.
Topic 3. Stress analysis of 3D parts.
teaching_methods: Autonomous learning from documents on the virtual platform
Case study-based learning for demonstrating specific procedures
Geometric modeling and simulation cases (CAD/CAE) for solving mechanical engineering problems using parametric 3D software (generally SolidWorks)
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 50% from item A1 and 50% from item A2. To pass the course, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required for both A1 and A2, along with a final minimum score of 5 out of 10. For the extraordinary examination, students who did not pass the practical component in the ordinary session will take a CAD practical exam (A2.2), while their A2.1 continuous assessment score is retained. The theoretical/practical exam (A1) will be similar to the ordinary session. The use of AI is prohibited for written exams (AIAS Level 1). For autonomous work, partial and assisted use of AI is allowed for idea generation/structuring (AIAS Level 2) and assisted editing (AIAS Level 3), but direct AI-generated text is not permitted, and declaration of AI use is mandatory.
